claim: During healthy urinary voiding, the bladder outflow tract dilates while detrusor smooth muscle in the bladder body contracts.

evidence: Supported by citations

claim: Accumulation of urine in the LUT predisposes to urosepsis in UFS.
source: Conversely, in UFS, voiding is incomplete because of dyssynergia in which the outflow tract fails to fully dilate (Ochoa, 2004), and subsequent accumulation of urine in the LUT predisposes to urosepsis (Ochoa, 2004; Osorio et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations

claim: UFS is an autosomal-recessive disease.

claim: Around half of UFS families studied genetically carry biallelic variants in HPSE2.

claim: Female Hpse2 mutant mice have neurogenic defects in outflow tract relaxation and detrusor contraction that are similar to those reported for male Hpse2 mutant mice.
source: First, female Hpse2 mutant mice have neurogenic defects in outflow tract relaxation and detrusor contraction that are similar to those reported for male Hpse2 mutant mice (Manak et al., 2020).
evidence: Comparison of current data with cited previous work

claim: Females displayed a more profound defect in contractions elicited by EFS compared to males.
source: For example, regarding bladder bodies, females displayed a more profound defect in contractions elicited by EFS, while they lacked the hyper-sensitivity to carbachol shown by males.
evidence: Comparison of data between male and female mice in the study

claim: Female mutant mice lacked the hyper-sensitivity to carbachol shown by males.
source: For example, regarding bladder bodies, females displayed a more profound defect in contractions elicited by EFS, while they lacked the hyper-sensitivity to carbachol shown by males.
evidence: Comparison of data between male and female mice in the study

claim: An AAV can be used to transduce pelvic ganglia.
source: Second, we have demonstrated that an AAV can be used to transduce pelvic ganglia that are key autonomic neuronal structures in the pathobiology of UFS.
evidence: Demonstrated by BaseScope ISH data in the study

claim: A single dose of 1 × 10^11 genome copies of AAV9/HPSE2 was sufficient to transduce around half of neural cell bodies in pelvic ganglia when assessed in the third postnatal week.
source: A single dose of 1 × 1011 genome copies of AAV9/HPSE2 was sufficient to transduce around half of neural cell bodies in these ganglia when assessed in the third postnatal week.
evidence: Quantification of BaseScope ISH data

claim: The administration of a higher dose of the vector would possibly have resulted in a higher percent of positive cell bodies.
source: It is possible that the administration of a higher dose of the vector would have resulted in a higher percent of positive cell bodies.
evidence: Speculation based on dose-response relationship observed

claim: The 1 × 10^11 dose significantly ameliorated defect in the mutant LUT despite not every neural cell body being transduced.
source: Our third key observation is that the 1 × 1011 dose significantly ameliorated defect in the mutant LUT despite not every neural cell body being transduced.
evidence: Combination of transduction data and functional myography data

claim: It will be important to study whether the gene transfer strategy might also ameliorate a dyssynergia between bladder and outflow as assessed by in vivo cystometry.
source: In future, it will be important to study whether the gene transfer strategy might also ameliorate a dyssynergia between bladder and outflow as assessed by in vivo cystometry (Ito et al., 2018).
evidence: Statement of future research direction

claim: The authors cannot yet rule out an additional myogenic component to defects in UFS bladder functionality.
source: Although our data support a neurogenic origin for defects in UFS bladder functionality, we cannot yet rule out an additional myogenic component.
evidence: Acknowledgment of limitation in interpretation

claim: No significant differences in smooth muscle actin (Acta2) and myosin heavy chain (Myh11) transcripts were recorded between WT and Hpse2 homozygous mutant mice at 1 and 14 days after birth.
source: In a previous study (Stuart et al., 2015), however, we quantified smooth muscle actin (Acta2) and myosin heavy chain (Myh11) transcripts at 1 and 14 days after birth and recorded no significant differences between WT and Hpse2 homozygous mutant mice.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work

claim: Detrusor smooth muscle itself is unchanged in the juvenile period in Hpse2 mutant mice.
source: This suggests that detrusor smooth muscle itself is unchanged in the juvenile period.
evidence: Inference from cited data on smooth muscle markers

claim: AAV9/HPSE2 was not detected transducing detrusor smooth muscle in the current study.
source: Moreover, in the current study, we did not detect transduction of AAV9/HPSE2 into detrusor smooth muscle.
evidence: BaseScope ISH data from the study

claim: A feature of the current mouse model is poor whole body growth compared with WT controls.
source: A feature of the current mouse model, also observed in a different Hpse2 gene trap mouse (Guo et al., 2015), is the poor whole body growth compared with WT controls.
evidence: Body weight data from the study and citation

claim: Poor whole body growth in Hpse2 mutant mice becomes more marked during the first month of life.
source: This becomes more marked during the first month of life, and, in the current study, it was not ameliorated by neonatal AAV9/HPSE2 administration.
evidence: Body weight data from the study

claim: Poor whole body growth in Hpse2 mutant mice was not ameliorated by neonatal AAV9/HPSE2 administration.
source: This becomes more marked during the first month of life, and, in the current study, it was not ameliorated by neonatal AAV9/HPSE2 administration.
evidence: Body weight data from the study

claim: The cause of the growth impairment in Hpse2 mutant mice has not been established.
source: The cause of the growth impairment has not been established, but, as demonstrated in the current study, is not accompanied by structural kidney damage.
evidence: Statement of knowledge gap

claim: Growth impairment in Hpse2 mutant mice is not accompanied by structural kidney damage.
source: The cause of the growth impairment has not been established, but, as demonstrated in the current study, is not accompanied by structural kidney damage.
evidence: Histology data from kidneys in the study

claim: Hpse2 mutant pups appear to feed normally, as assessed by finding their stomachs full of mother's milk.
source: Moreover, our unpublished observations found that Hpse2 mutant pups appear to feed normally, as assessed by finding their stomachs full of mother's milk.
evidence: Unpublished observational data

claim: Histological examination of Hpse2 mutant lungs is normal, excluding aspiration pneumonia.
source: Histological examination of their lungs is normal, excluding aspiration pneumonia.
evidence: Histology data

claim: The general growth failure in Hpse2 mutant mice is dissociated from the LUT phenotype.
source: Whatever the cause of the general growth failure, it is notably dissociated from the LUT phenotype, given that AAV9/HPSE2 administration corrects bladder pathophysiology but not overall growth of the mutant mouse.
evidence: Comparison of body weight and bladder function data

claim: A recently published study induced deletion of Hpse2 in young adult mice, followed by fatty degeneration of pancreatic acinar cells.
source: Of note, a recently published study induced deletion of Hpse2 in young adult mice (Kayal et al., 2023), and this was followed by fatty degeneration of pancreatic acinar cells.
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: A small subset of individuals with UFS carry biallelic variants of leucine-rich repeats and immunoglobulin-like domains 2 (LRIG2).
source: A small subset of individuals with UFS carry biallelic variants of leucine-rich repeats and immunoglobulin-like domains 2 (LRIG2) (Stuart et al., 2013; Grenier et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations

claim: LRIG2, like heparanase-2, is immunodetected in pelvic ganglia.
source: LRIG2, like heparanase-2, is immunodetected in pelvic ganglia (Stuart et al., 2013; Roberts et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations

claim: Homozygous Lrig2 mutant mice have abnormal patterns of bladder nerves and display ex vivo contractility defects in LUT tissues compatible with neurogenic pathobiology.
source: Moreover, homozygous Lrig2 mutant mice have abnormal patterns of bladder nerves and display ex vivo contractility defects in LUT tissues compatible with neurogenic pathobiology (Roberts et al., 2019; Grenier et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations

claim: Functional bladder outflow obstruction occurs in some individuals with prune belly syndrome.
source: As well as in UFS, functional bladder outflow obstruction occurs in some individuals with prune belly syndrome (Volmar et al., 2001) and in megacystis microcolon intestinal hypoperistalsis syndrome (Gosemann and Puri, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: Functional bladder outflow obstruction occurs in megacystis microcolon intestinal hypoperistalsis syndrome.
source: As well as in UFS, functional bladder outflow obstruction occurs in some individuals with prune belly syndrome (Volmar et al., 2001) and in megacystis microcolon intestinal hypoperistalsis syndrome (Gosemann and Puri, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: Neonatal mice are immature compared to a newborn person.
source: First, neonatal mice are immature compared to a newborn person, and the anatomy of their still developing kidneys and LUTs can be compared to those organs in the human foetus in the late second trimester (Lopes and Woolf, 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: The anatomy of neonatal mouse kidneys and LUTs can be compared to those organs in the human foetus in the late second trimester.
source: First, neonatal mice are immature compared to a newborn person, and the anatomy of their still developing kidneys and LUTs can be compared to those organs in the human foetus in the late second trimester (Lopes and Woolf, 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: Gene replacement therapy for people with UFS and related genetic REOLUT disorders may need to be given before birth.
source: Thus, gene replacement therapy for people with UFS and related genetic REOLUT disorders may need to be given before birth.
evidence: Inference from developmental timing comparison

claim: UFS can present in the fetal period when ultrasonography reveals a dilated LUT.
source: In fact, UFS can present in the fetal period when ultrasonography reveals a dilated LUT (Grenier et al., 2023; Grenier et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations

claim: Human gene therapy with AAV9 vectors has been associated with liver damage.
source: Given that human gene therapy with AAV9 vectors has been associated with a specific side effect, liver damage (Mendell et al., 2017), and the recent implication of AAV2 in community-acquired hepatitis (Ho et al., 2023), we also examined mouse livers at the end of the experiment.
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: AAV2 has been recently implicated in community-acquired hepatitis.
source: Given that human gene therapy with AAV9 vectors has been associated with a specific side effect, liver damage (Mendell et al., 2017), and the recent implication of AAV2 in community-acquired hepatitis (Ho et al., 2023), we also examined mouse livers at the end of the experiment.
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: The dose of AAV9 vector administered to the Hpse2 mutant mice in the current study is of a similar order of magnitude as those used to treat babies with spinal muscular atrophy, factoring weight for weight.
source: Factoring weight for weight, the dose of AAV9 vector administered to the Hpse2 mutant mice in the current study is of a similar order of magnitude as those used to treat babies with spinal muscular atrophy (Mendell et al., 2017).
evidence: Comparison with cited clinical trial data

claim: In the spinal muscular atrophy treatment report, there was evidence of liver damage, as assessed by raised blood transaminases in a subset of treated patients.
source: In that report there was evidence of liver damage, as assessed by raised blood transaminases in a subset of treated patients.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mendell et al., 2017

claim: The viral vector transduced livers in the current mouse study.
source: In the current mouse study, we found that the viral vector transduced livers, while kidneys were resistant to transduction.
evidence: BaseScope ISH data from the study

claim: Kidneys were resistant to transduction by the viral vector in the current study.
source: In the current mouse study, we found that the viral vector transduced livers, while kidneys were resistant to transduction.
evidence: BaseScope ISH data from the study

claim: The authors cannot exclude transient liver damage in AAV9/HPSE2-treated mice, which could be assessed by alterations in blood transaminases.
source: We cannot, however, exclude transient liver damage, which could be assessed by alterations in blood transaminases.
evidence: Acknowledgment of limitation in the study

claim: Heparanase-2 is a secreted protein.
source: The fact that transduced livers expressed HPSE2 transcripts, and the observation that heparanse-2 is a secreted protein (Levy-Adam et al., 2010; Beaman et al., 2022), raises the possibility that the livers of treated mice may act as a factory to produce heparanase-2 that then circulated and had beneficial effects on the LUT, akin to gene therapy to replace coagulation factors missing in haemophilia (Chowdary et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations

claim: The livers of treated mice may act as a factory to produce heparanase-2 that then circulated and had beneficial effects on the LUT.
source: The fact that transduced livers expressed HPSE2 transcripts, and the observation that heparanse-2 is a secreted protein (Levy-Adam et al., 2010; Beaman et al., 2022), raises the possibility that the livers of treated mice may act as a factory to produce heparanase-2 that then circulated and had beneficial effects on the LUT, akin to gene therapy to replace coagulation factors missing in haemophilia (Chowdary et al., 2022).
evidence: Speculation based on liver transduction data and known protein secretion

claim: The mutant allele has the retroviral gene trap VICTR4829 vector inserted into intron 6 of Hpse2.
source: The mutant allele has the retroviral gene trap VICTR4829 vector inserted into intron 6 of Hpse2 (Stuart et al., 2015) (mouse accession NM_001081257 and Omnibank clone OST441123).
evidence: Description of the genetic mutation with citation

claim: The mutation is predicted to splice exon 6 to a Neo cassette and generate a premature stop codon.
source: The mutation is predicted to splice exon 6 to a Neo cassette and generate a premature stop codon.
evidence: Prediction based on the nature of the gene trap insertion

claim: Homozygous mutant mouse bladder tissue contains a truncated Hpse2 transcript and lacks full-length Hpse2 transcripts extending beyond the trap.
source: Accordingly, homozygous mutant mouse bladder tissue contains a truncated Hpse2 transcript and lacks full-length Hpse2 transcripts extending beyond the trap (Stuart et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: Mating heterozygous parents leads to the birth of WT, heterozygous, and Mut offspring in the expected Mendelian ratio.
source: Mating heterozygous parents leads to the birth of WT, heterozygous, and Mut offspring in the expected Mendelian ratio (Stuart et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: In the first month after birth, Mut mice gain less weight than their WT littermates.
source: In the first month after birth, Mut mice gain less weight than their WT littermates (Stuart et al., 2015) and, because they later fail to thrive, Mut mice are culled around a month of age before they become overtly unwell.
evidence: Supported by citation and data in current study

claim: Mut mice are culled around a month of age before they become overtly unwell because they fail to thrive.
source: In the first month after birth, Mut mice gain less weight than their WT littermates (Stuart et al., 2015) and, because they later fail to thrive, Mut mice are culled around a month of age before they become overtly unwell.
evidence: Description of experimental animal husbandry practice

claim: Sympathetic stimulation of α-1 adrenergic receptors mediates urethral contraction in male mice and primates but has little effect in females.
source: Sympathetic stimulation of α-1 adrenergic receptors mediates urethral contraction in male mice and primates but has little effect in females (Alexandre et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: Female outflow tracts express contractile arginine-vasopressin (AVP) receptors.
source: Female outflow tracts were instead pre-contracted with vasopressin (10 nM) as previously detailed (Grenier et al., 2023) because they are known to express contractile arginine-vasopressin (AVP) receptors (Zeng et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation

claim: Bladder body contractions are primarily mediated by acetylcholine, through its release from parasympathetic nerves and binding to muscarinic receptors.
source: As these contractions are primarily mediated by acetylcholine, through its release from parasympathetic nerves and binding to muscarinic receptors (Matsui et al., 2002), we also measured the degree of bladder body contractions evoked directly by the muscarinic agonist, carbachol (10 nM to 50 μM).
evidence: Supported by citation
